nodes.summary: Given a Fibonacci tree $t$ and a list of Fibonacci trees, the insertion of $t$ into the list is defined recursively. Inserting $t$ into the empty list gives the one-tree list $[t]$. For a list with first tree $s$ and remaining list $L$: if the stored degree of $t$ is less than the stored degree of $s$, the result is $t$ followed by $s$ and then $L$; if the two stored degrees are equal, the result is the insertion…
nodes.title: Inserting a tree into a forest

nodes.summary: For every Fibonacci heap $H$ and every value $x$, the number of elements of the heap obtained by inserting $x$ into $H$, counted with multiplicity, is the number of elements of $H$ plus one.
nodes.title: Insertion increases the size of a Fibonacci heap by one

nodes.summary: For Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$, the number of elements of the meld of $H_1$ and $H_2$, counted with multiplicity, is the number of elements of $H_1$ plus the number of elements of $H_2$.
nodes.title: Melding adds the sizes of Fibonacci heaps

nodes.summary: Every Fibonacci tree represents at least one element: the multiset of elements of any Fibonacci tree has positive size.
nodes.title: Fibonacci trees are nonempty

nodes.summary: Every child of a valid Fibonacci tree is itself a valid Fibonacci tree.
nodes.title: Children of a valid Fibonacci tree are valid

nodes.summary: The children of the Fibonacci tree with stored degree $d$, root value $r$ and list of subtrees $c$ are the trees of the list $c$, in order.
nodes.title: Children of a Fibonacci tree

nodes.summary: For every list of Fibonacci trees, the trees in its consolidation have pairwise distinct stored degrees.
nodes.title: Consolidation yields distinct root degrees

nodes.summary: For every list of Fibonacci trees, the stored degrees of the trees in its consolidation are strictly increasing in list order.
nodes.title: Consolidation sorts root degrees

nodes.summary: The consolidation of a list of Fibonacci trees is defined recursively: the consolidation of the empty list is the empty list, and the consolidation of a list with first tree $t$ and remaining list $L$ is the insertion of $t$ into the consolidation of $L$.
nodes.title: Consolidation of a forest

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fibonacci tree and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ and leaves a remainder tree $t'$, then the multiset of elements of $t$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $t'$ and of $s$.
nodes.title: Cutting a subtree splits the elements of a Fibonacci tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fibonacci tree and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ and leaves no remainder, then $s = t$.
nodes.title: A cut without remainder extracts the whole tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a valid Fibonacci tree over a type with a relation $\le$, and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree and leaves a remainder tree $t'$, then $t'$ is valid: its children are valid, its stored degree equals its number of children, and its root is $\le$ every element of $t'$.
nodes.title: The remainder of a cut from a valid tree is valid

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a valid Fibonacci tree over a type with a relation $\le$, and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ (with or without a remainder), then $s$ is valid.
nodes.title: The subtree extracted by a cut from a valid tree is valid

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fibonacci tree and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ (with or without a remainder), then $s$ is the subtree of $t$ at $p$.
nodes.title: A cut extracts the addressed subtree

nodes.summary: For a path $p$ of child indices and a Fibonacci tree $t$, the cut of $t$ at $p$ is either undefined or a pair of an extracted subtree and an optional remainder tree. For the empty path, the extracted subtree is $t$ and there is no remainder. For a path consisting of an index $i$ followed by a path $q$, where $t$ has root $r$ and children $c_0, \dots, c_{k-1}$, the cut is undefined if $i \ge k$ or if the cut of…
nodes.title: Cutting a subtree out of a Fibonacci tree

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a forest of Fibonacci trees, $i$ an index and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $F$ at the $i$-th tree and path $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ and leaves the forest $F'$, then the multiset of elements of $F$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $F'$ and of $s$.
nodes.title: Cutting a subtree splits the elements of a Fibonacci forest

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a forest of Fibonacci trees whose tree at position $i$ is $t$, and let $p$ be a path of child indices such that the subtree of $t$ at $p$ is $s$. Then cutting $F$ at index $i$ and path $p$ is defined and extracts $s$, together with some remaining forest.
nodes.title: Every addressed subtree of a forest can be cut out

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a valid forest of Fibonacci trees over a type with a relation $\le$, $i$ an index and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $F$ at index $i$ and path $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ and leaves the forest $F'$, then $s$ is a valid tree and $F'$ is a valid forest.
nodes.title: Cutting a valid forest leaves valid parts

nodes.summary: For a forest given as a list of Fibonacci trees, an index $i$ and a path $p$ of child indices, the cut is undefined if the list has no tree at position $i$ (counting from $0$) or if cutting that tree $t$ at $p$ is undefined. Otherwise, if cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts the subtree $s$, the result is $s$ together with the list in which the tree at position $i$ is removed (if the cut of $t$ left no remainder) or…
nodes.title: Cutting a subtree out of a Fibonacci forest

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index, $p$ a path of child indices and $k$ a key. Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds and extracts the subtree $S$, and that $k$ is at most the root of $S$. Then the multiset represented by the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ has the same number of elements,…
nodes.title: Decrease-key preserves the number of elements

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, let $T$ be the $i$-th tree of its root list, and let $S$ be the subtree of $T$ at the path $p$ of child indices. If the key $k$ is at most the root of $S$, then the multiset represented by the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ is the multiset represented by $H$ with one occurrence of the root of $S$ removed and one occurrence of $k$ added.
nodes.title: Decrease-key replaces one key, stated by address

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index, $p$ a path of child indices and $k$ a key. Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds and extracts the subtree $S$, and that $k$ is at most the root of $S$. Then the multiset represented by the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ is the multiset represented by $H$…
nodes.title: Decrease-key replaces one key

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ fails, then for every key $k$, decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ returns $H$ unchanged.
nodes.title: Decrease-key at an unresolved address does nothing

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index, $p$ a path of child indices and $k$ a key. Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds and extracts the subtree $S$, and that $k$ is not at most the root of $S$ (keys are linearly ordered, so $k$ is greater than that root). Then decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ returns $H$ unchanged.
nodes.title: Decrease-key with a larger key does nothing

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap whose minimum, as returned by find-min, is $m$, and let $i$ be a root index, $p$ a path of child indices and $k$ a key. Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds and extracts the subtree $S$, and that $k$ is at most the root of $S$. Then find-min on the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$…
nodes.title: Minimum after decrease-key

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index, $p$ a path of child indices and $k$ a key. Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds, extracting the subtree $S$ and leaving the forest $R$, and that $k$ is at most the root of $S$. Then the root list of the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ consists of $S$ with…
nodes.title: Root list after decrease-key

nodes.summary: For every Fibonacci heap $H$, root index $i$, path $p$ of child indices and key $k$, the root list of the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ is a valid forest, that is, every tree in it is valid.
nodes.title: Decrease-key yields a valid forest

nodes.summary: Given a Fibonacci heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, a root index $i$, a path $p$ of child indices and a key $k$, decrease-key cuts the subtree $S$ at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$, replaces the root of $S$ by $k$, and puts the resulting tree in front of the remaining forest (the root list with the $i$-th tree replaced by what is left of it after the cut, or removed when $S$ is that…
nodes.title: Decrease-key in a Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a valid Fibonacci tree over a preordered type and let $k$ be a key that is at most the root of $T$. Then the tree obtained from $T$ by replacing its root by $k$, keeping its degree and children, is valid: the new root is still no greater than every represented element.
nodes.title: Lowering the root keeps a Fibonacci tree valid

nodes.summary: For a Fibonacci tree $t$ and a key $k$, this is the tree whose root value is $k$ and whose stored degree and list of children are those of $t$.
nodes.title: Replacing the root key of a Fibonacci tree

nodes.summary: For every valid Fibonacci tree, its stored degree equals the number of its children.
nodes.title: The degree of a valid Fibonacci tree is its number of children

nodes.summary: If two Fibonacci trees $s$ and $t$ over a linearly ordered type have the same degree $d$, then their link has degree $d + 1$.
nodes.title: Degree of the link of two trees of equal degree

nodes.summary: For every valid Fibonacci tree over a type with a relation $\le$, the degree of the tree is strictly less than the number of elements, counted with multiplicity, of the multiset the tree represents, since every child contributes at least one element.
nodes.title: The degree of a valid Fibonacci tree is less than its size

nodes.summary: The degree of the Fibonacci tree with stored degree $d$, root value $r$ and list of children $c$ is the stored natural number $d$; it is not computed from the children.
nodes.title: Degree of a Fibonacci tree

nodes.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap $H$ succeeds and returns the value $m$ and the heap $H'$, then the multiset of elements of $H$ is the multiset of elements of $H'$ with one copy of $m$ added.
nodes.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion splits off the minimum

nodes.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap $H$ succeeds and returns the value $m$ and the heap $H'$, then the multiset of elements of $H'$ is the multiset of elements of $H$ with one occurrence of $m$ removed.
nodes.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion removes one copy of the minimum

nodes.summary: Deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap fails if and only if the heap's list of root trees is empty.
nodes.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion fails exactly on the empty heap

nodes.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap $H$ succeeds and returns the value $m$, then $m \le v$ for every element $v$ of $H$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion returns a lower bound

nodes.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap succeeds and returns the heap $H'$, then the number of root trees of $H'$ is at most the number of elements of $H'$, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: After minimum deletion a Fibonacci heap has at most as many roots as elements

nodes.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap succeeds and returns the heap $H'$, then the degrees of the root trees of $H'$, in list order, are strictly increasing; consolidation is what makes them so.
nodes.title: Minimum deletion leaves a Fibonacci heap with strictly increasing root degrees

nodes.summary: For every Fibonacci heap $H$, deleting the minimum of $H$ and keeping only the returned value and the root list of the resulting heap gives the same result as the root-list minimum deletion applied to the root list of $H$: either both fail, or both return the same value and the same list of trees.
nodes.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion agrees with its root-list version

nodes.summary: Given a list of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, the result is nothing if the list is empty. Otherwise the first tree whose root is minimal is removed, and the result is its root value together with the consolidation of the forest made of the removed tree's children followed by the remaining trees.
nodes.title: Minimum deletion on a forest

nodes.summary: If the root list of the heap is empty, the result is nothing. Otherwise the first tree of the root list whose root is minimal is removed, and the result is its root value together with the heap whose root list is the consolidation of the removed tree's children followed by the remaining trees, and whose cached minimum is the minimum root of this consolidated forest.
nodes.title: Deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: Write $M(t)$ for the multiset of values stored in a Fibonacci tree $t$. The multiset represented by a Fibonacci forest, a list of Fibonacci trees $t_1, \dots, t_k$, is the sum $M(t_1) + \cdots + M(t_k)$; the empty forest represents the empty multiset.
nodes.title: Multiset of a Fibonacci forest

nodes.summary: The multiset represented by a Fibonacci heap over a linearly ordered type is the multiset of its list of trees: the sum, over the trees in the list, of the multisets of values stored in them. The cached minimum plays no role.
nodes.title: Multiset of a Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: For any two lists $L$ and $R$ of Fibonacci trees, the forest made of the trees of $L$ followed by the trees of $R$ represents the sum of the multisets represented by $L$ and by $R$.
nodes.title: Elements of a concatenated forest

nodes.summary: For every list of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, its consolidation represents the same multiset as the original list.
nodes.title: Consolidation preserves the elements

nodes.summary: For a Fibonacci tree $t$ and any key $k$, the multiset of elements represented by the tree obtained from $t$ by replacing its root value with $k$ equals the multiset of elements of $t$ with one occurrence of the root of $t$ removed and $k$ added.
nodes.title: Elements after replacing the root key

nodes.summary: The empty Fibonacci heap represents the empty multiset.
nodes.title: The empty Fibonacci heap has no elements

nodes.summary: For every Fibonacci heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type and every value $x$, the heap obtained by inserting $x$ into $H$ represents the multiset of $H$ with one more occurrence of $x$.
nodes.title: Insertion adds one occurrence

nodes.summary: For any two Fibonacci trees $S$ and $T$ over a linearly ordered type, the tree obtained by linking $S$ and $T$ represents the sum of the multisets represented by $S$ and by $T$.
nodes.title: Linking adds the elements

nodes.summary: For any two Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ over a linearly ordered type, the meld of $H_1$ and $H_2$ represents the sum of the multisets represented by $H_1$ and by $H_2$.
nodes.title: Melding adds the elements

nodes.summary: For every value $x$ of a linearly ordered type, the singleton Fibonacci heap on $x$, whose only tree is the single-node tree with root $x$, represents the multiset $\{x\}$.
nodes.title: Multiset of a singleton Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: For Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ over a linearly ordered type, the multiset represented by the union of $H_1$ and $H_2$ is the sum of the multisets represented by $H_1$ and by $H_2$.
nodes.title: The union of Fibonacci heaps adds their multisets

nodes.summary: The multiset $M(t)$ of values stored in a Fibonacci tree $t$, defined recursively: if $t$ has root value $r$ and children $t_1, \dots, t_k$, then $M(t) = \{r\} + M(t_1) + \cdots + M(t_k)$. The stored degree plays no role.
nodes.title: Multiset of a Fibonacci tree

nodes.summary: The Fibonacci heap over a linearly ordered type whose list of trees is empty and whose cached minimum is absent.
nodes.title: Empty Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: A Fibonacci min-heap over a linearly ordered type consists of a list of Fibonacci trees, each valid (heap-ordered, and at every node the stored degree equals the number of children), together with a cached minimum equal to the least root value of these trees, absent when the list is empty.
nodes.title: Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: A Fibonacci tree over a type $\alpha$ is a rose tree: a node carrying a stored degree $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a root value in $\alpha$, and a finite list of child Fibonacci trees.
nodes.title: Fibonacci tree

nodes.summary: For a Fibonacci heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, find-min on $H$ returns no value if and only if $H$ has no trees.
nodes.title: Find-min fails exactly on the empty Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap over a linearly ordered type. If find-min on $H$ returns $m$, then $m \le v$ for every value $v$ in the multiset represented by $H$.
nodes.title: Find-min returns a lower bound of the Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap over a linearly ordered type. If find-min on $H$ returns $m$, then $m$ belongs to the multiset represented by $H$.
nodes.title: Find-min returns an element of the Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: Find-min on a Fibonacci heap returns its cached minimum without modifying the heap: the least root value of its trees, or no value when the heap has no trees.
nodes.title: Find-min for Fibonacci heaps

nodes.summary: Inserting a value $x$ into a Fibonacci heap $H$ gives the meld of the one-element Fibonacci heap containing $x$ with $H$, the one-element heap coming first.
nodes.title: Insertion into a Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a valid forest of Fibonacci trees whose degrees are strictly increasing along the list. Then the number of trees in $F$ is at most the number of elements, counted with multiplicity, that $F$ represents.
nodes.title: Degree-sorted forests have at most as many trees as elements

nodes.summary: If $s$ and $t$ are valid Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, then the link of $s$ and $t$ is a valid Fibonacci tree.
nodes.title: Linking preserves validity of Fibonacci trees

nodes.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type. If the root of $s$ is at most the root of $t$, the link of $s$ and $t$ is the tree with the root of $s$, stored degree one more than that of $s$, and children $t$ followed by the children of $s$. Otherwise it is the tree with the root of $t$, stored degree one more than that of $t$, and children $s$ followed by the children of $t$.
nodes.title: Linking two Fibonacci trees

nodes.summary: The meld of Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ is the Fibonacci heap whose root list is the root list of $H_1$ followed by that of $H_2$, and whose cached minimum is the smaller of the two cached minima when both heaps have one, and otherwise the cached minimum of whichever heap has one (none if neither does).
nodes.title: Melding Fibonacci heaps

nodes.summary: For optional values $x$ and $y$ of a linearly ordered type, their combined minimum is defined as follows: if $x$ and $y$ are both present, with values $a$ and $b$, it is $\min(a, b)$; if exactly one of $x$ and $y$ is present, it is that value; and if both are absent, it is absent.
nodes.title: Minimum of two optional values

nodes.summary: For forests $F$ and $G$ of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, the minimum root of $F$ followed by $G$ is the combined minimum of the optional minimum roots of $F$ and of $G$: their minimum if both exist, the one that exists if only one does, and absent if neither does.
nodes.title: Minimum root of a concatenated forest

nodes.summary: A forest of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type has no minimum root exactly when it is empty.
nodes.title: Only the empty forest has no minimum root

nodes.summary: If a forest $F$ of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type has minimum root $m$, then $m$ is the root of some tree of $F$ and $m$ is at most the root of every tree of $F$.
nodes.title: The minimum root is a least root

nodes.summary: The minimum root of a forest of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type is an optional value: it is absent for the empty forest, and for a nonempty forest it is the least of the roots of its trees.
nodes.title: Minimum root of a forest

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a list of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type. If removing a minimum tree from $T$ returns a tree $m$ and a list $R$, then the multiset of elements of $m$ plus the multiset of elements of $R$ equals the multiset of elements of $T$, the tree $m$ belongs to $T$, the list $R$ is a sublist of $T$, and the root of $m$ is at most the root of every tree in $T$.
nodes.title: Minimum-tree removal in a Fibonacci forest

nodes.summary: For a list of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, this returns nothing on the empty list. Otherwise it returns the first tree whose root is minimal among all roots in the list, so earlier trees win ties, together with the list of the remaining trees in their original order.
nodes.title: Removing a minimum tree from a Fibonacci forest

nodes.summary: The root of a valid Fibonacci tree is no greater than every element of the multiset the tree represents.
nodes.title: Roots of valid Fibonacci trees are lower bounds

nodes.summary: For every Fibonacci tree, its root value belongs to the multiset of elements the tree represents.
nodes.title: The root of a Fibonacci tree is one of its elements

nodes.summary: The root of a Fibonacci tree is the value stored at its top node.
nodes.title: Root of a Fibonacci tree

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ of a linearly ordered type, the singleton Fibonacci heap on $x$ has as its only tree the single-node tree with root $x$, stored degree $0$ and no children, and its cached minimum is $x$.
nodes.title: Singleton Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ of a linearly ordered type, the one-element Fibonacci heap on $x$ has as its only tree the single-node tree with root $x$, and its cached minimum is $x$.
nodes.title: One-element Fibonacci heap

nodes.summary: A Fibonacci forest, a list of Fibonacci trees $t_1, \dots, t_k$, has sorted degrees when the stored degrees of its trees strictly increase along the list: $\deg t_i < \deg t_j$ whenever $i < j$.
nodes.title: Forests with strictly increasing degrees

nodes.summary: If a list of Fibonacci trees is a valid forest, then every sublist of it (a subsequence, not necessarily contiguous) is a valid forest.
nodes.title: Sublists of valid Fibonacci forests are valid

nodes.summary: If a Fibonacci tree $t$ is valid and a path $p$ of child indices addresses a subtree $s$ of $t$, then $s$ is valid.
nodes.title: Subtrees of a valid Fibonacci tree are valid

nodes.summary: If a path $p$ of child indices addresses a subtree $s$ of a Fibonacci tree $t$, then cutting $t$ at $p$ succeeds and extracts exactly $s$, together with some remainder, which may be absent.
nodes.title: Every addressed subtree can be cut out

nodes.summary: For a list $p = (i_1, \dots, i_n)$ of natural numbers and a Fibonacci tree $t$, the subtree of $t$ at $p$ is found by starting at the root and moving to the child with zero-based index $i_1$, then to its child with index $i_2$, and so on. The result is absent when some index is at least the number of children of the current node. The empty path addresses the whole tree $t$.
nodes.title: Subtree of a Fibonacci tree at a path

nodes.summary: The union of Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ is their meld: the heap whose trees are those of $H_1$ followed by those of $H_2$, and whose cached minimum is the smaller of the two cached minima (the one that exists if a heap is empty, none if both are).
nodes.title: Union of Fibonacci heaps

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ carry a relation $\le$. A Fibonacci forest, a list of Fibonacci trees with values in $\alpha$, is valid when every tree in it is a valid Fibonacci tree.
nodes.title: Valid Fibonacci forests

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ carry a relation $\le$. If $F$ and $G$ are valid Fibonacci forests with values in $\alpha$, then the forest consisting of the trees of $F$ followed by the trees of $G$ is valid.
nodes.title: Concatenation preserves validity of Fibonacci forests

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. If a Fibonacci forest with values in $\alpha$ is valid, then its consolidation is valid.
nodes.title: Consolidation preserves validity

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ carry a relation $\le$. The empty forest, containing no Fibonacci trees with values in $\alpha$, is valid.
nodes.title: The empty Fibonacci forest is valid

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every $v \in \alpha$, the Fibonacci tree of degree $0$ with root $v$ and no children is valid.
nodes.title: Singleton Fibonacci trees are valid

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ carry a relation $\le$. A Fibonacci tree with stored degree $d$, root $r \in \alpha$ and list of children $c$ is valid when every tree in $c$ is valid, $d$ equals the length of $c$, and $r \le x$ for every element $x$ of the multiset represented by the tree (the root together with the elements of all children).
nodes.title: Valid Fibonacci trees

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
